METHOD & LIMITATIONS

A citation graph, not a verdict.

Topic influence uses personalized PageRank on the citation graph inside this collection. A paper receives more influence when other influential papers cite it. Selecting a topic concentrates the restart probability on papers tagged with that topic.

01 · Citation links

Edges point from a citing paper to a cited paper. Only actual, retrieved Semantic Scholar reference links between catalog records are used. Duplicate links and self-links are removed.

02 · Topic personalization

At each step, 85% of influence follows citation links and 15% restarts uniformly among papers in the selected topic. Papers with no in-catalog references redistribute their influence using the same restart distribution.

03 · Read the score

The highest-ranked paper in the selected topic is shown as 100. Other scores are relative to it, not quality ratings or percentages of all citations. Keyword and author searches filter these topic rankings without changing their meaning.

Formula, coverage, and reproducibility

r = 0.85 Pᵀr + 0.15 v

P follows in-catalog references; dangling rows equal v. The restart vector v is uniform over papers tagged with the selected topic (or all papers when no topic is selected). Iteration stops at L1 change below 10⁻¹⁰ or 200 iterations.

The graph is incomplete: citations to papers outside the collection are not followed. Unretrieved references are not evidence of no references. New papers, missing records, topic-label errors, and collection selection can affect ranks. Scores are exploratory, not a global measure of scientific importance.

Global citation counts are supplied separately by Semantic Scholar, with a retrieval date on each paper. “Unavailable” means no verified count was retrieved—not zero. Counts and reference data are snapshots, not a live feed.

ABOUT THE COLLECTION

A starting point for careful reading.

This library combines the supplied arXiv AI safety and security collection with foundational reward-hacking papers discussed in the literature review and new arXiv submissions discovered by the updater. It includes attacks, defenses, evaluations, and conceptual work—not just demonstrated attacks.

Broad topic labels come from automated screening. New arrivals are marked Auto-screened; inclusion is not an assessment of their quality or attack success. Reward-hacking annotations distinguish abstract-level screening from full-text evidence. A black-box label for a target model does not automatically imply black-box access to its reward function; inspect the paper’s methods before relying on that classification.

arXiv update status

Only new submissions matching the configured AI safety and security topics are considered. Citation counts may take time to appear. This index is not endorsed by arXiv.
